The IP address is used for security monitoring, geographic analysis, and detecting suspicious login patterns. It helps identify potential security threats and provides forensic data for incident investigation.

href.description:
Connection URL where the session was created. This field records the exact URL that the user was accessing when the session was established.

The href field provides context about the user's navigation path and helps understand session creation patterns. It is valuable for user experience analysis and troubleshooting connection issues.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL that directed to the session creation. This field captures the previous page URL that led the user to the session creation point.

The referrer information helps track user navigation flows and understand how users arrive at authentication points. It supports marketing analytics and user journey optimization.

created_at.description:
Timestamp when the session was created. This field records the exact date and time when the session was established in the system.

The creation timestamp is used for session lifecycle management, expiration tracking, and audit trail purposes. It helps determine session validity and supports compliance reporting.

expired_at.description:
Timestamp when the session expired. Null if still active. This field indicates when the session became invalid due to timeout or explicit logout.

Expired sessions are retained for audit purposes but are no longer valid for authentication. The expiration mechanism supports security best practices by automatically terminating inactive sessions.

ITodoAppUserSession.description:
User authentication sessions for tracking login activity and maintaining security context.

Stores comprehensive session information for authenticated users including connection context, timestamps, and relationship data. Each session represents a single login instance and serves as the foundation for audit tracing of user actions throughout the application.

Sessions are managed through sophisticated identity flows and include automatic expiration mechanisms to ensure security compliance. The system supports multiple concurrent sessions per user across different devices, enabling flexible access patterns while maintaining security controls.

Connection context fields (ip, href, referrer) provide essential security monitoring capabilities and support forensic analysis. These fields help detect suspicious activity patterns, track user navigation behavior, and maintain compliance with security standards.

The session lifecycle is carefully managed with creation and expiration timestamps that support both real-time session validation and historical audit requirements. This entity integrates with the broader authentication system to provide a complete security framework for the Todo application.

ITodoAppConfiguration.IRequest.description:

This DTO provides comprehensive search capabilities for configuration management operations, supporting text search, category filtering, data type filtering, pagination, and sorting.

The search functionality allows administrators to efficiently locate specific configuration settings or browse configuration items by category and type. Pagination ensures efficient handling of large configuration sets while maintaining performance.

Sorting options enable administrators to organize configuration settings by key, category, or modification timestamps for better management and oversight.

ITodoAppConfiguration.description:
Complete configuration setting entity representing system-wide configuration parameters for the Todo application.

This schema includes all fields from the Prisma database model, providing a complete representation of configuration settings with proper type mappings and validation. Configuration settings control application behavior, feature flags, and system parameters that affect the entire application instance.

Each configuration item has a unique key-value pair with associated metadata including data type specification, category organization, and audit timestamps. The schema ensures data integrity by mapping all database fields accurately and providing comprehensive documentation for each property.

Configuration settings are managed by administrators and may require application restart or specific refresh mechanisms to take effect when modified.

ITodoAppConfiguration.ISummary.description:
Summary view of configuration settings for list displays and quick reference in the Todo application.

This lightweight DTO provides essential configuration information for UI lists and overview displays, excluding detailed descriptions and audit timestamps to improve performance and reduce payload size.

The summary includes the core identifying information (key, value, category, data type) needed for administrators to quickly identify and reference configuration settings without loading the full configuration details.

This schema is optimized for paginated list operations and search results where complete configuration details are not immediately required.

ITodoAppConfiguration.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying existing configuration settings in the Todo application.

This DTO enables partial updates of configuration settings, allowing administrators to modify individual fields without requiring complete re-submission of all data. All fields are optional to support flexible update scenarios.

When updating configuration values, the system validates that the new value conforms to the specified data type. Changing the data type of an existing configuration may require additional validation to ensure compatibility with the current value.

Security considerations include requiring appropriate administrative permissions to modify system configuration settings, as changes can impact application functionality and feature availability.

ITodoAppUser.ISummary.description:
Summary view of user account information for reference purposes.

Provides essential user details needed for display contexts where complete user information is required but full user details would be excessive. Includes key identification and display fields optimized for list views and embedded references.

ITodoAppUser.IUpdate.description:

ITodoAppUserSession.IRequest.description:
Search criteria and pagination parameters for session filtering.

Provides comprehensive filtering options for retrieving user sessions based on multiple criteria including session status, creation date ranges, IP address patterns, and sorting preferences.

Pagination parameters ensure efficient retrieval of large session datasets with configurable page sizes. Status filtering allows users to view active sessions, expired sessions, or all sessions regardless of status.

ITodoAppTodo.description:
Core todo items with immutable attributes and ownership information.

Stores the fundamental, immutable attributes of todo items that remain constant throughout their lifecycle. This table contains the core business data that defines what the todo is, while mutable state information is handled through separate lifecycle and snapshot tables.

Each todo is owned by a specific user and created through an authenticated session for audit tracing. The immutable attributes include the todo's title, description, and creation context, while status, priority, and completion tracking are managed through normalized reference tables.

This separation ensures proper normalization and enables comprehensive audit trails through the snapshot pattern. Soft deletion is supported while maintaining data integrity and recovery capability.

The user and userSession relationships provide ownership context and audit trail information for each todo item.

ITodoAppUserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary view of user session information for audit, security, and reference purposes.

Provides essential session details needed for security monitoring, audit trail contexts, and session management interfaces where session information is required but full session details would be excessive. Includes key identification, timing, and connection context fields optimized for security and audit displays.

Integrates with the todo_app_user_sessions Prisma schema to ensure all essential session fields are available, maintaining proper security boundaries while providing sufficient session identification and audit trail capabilities for compliance and monitoring operations.

Used when displaying session information in security dashboards, audit trails, or other scenarios where session context is needed for security compliance, user activity tracking, and connection monitoring across the application ecosystem.

id.description: Primary key identifier for the user session. Unique across all session records in the system, generated automatically using UUID v4.

ip.description: IP address of the connection that created this session. Used for security monitoring, geographic tracking, and identifying potential security threats or unauthorized access attempts.

href.description: Connection URL where the session was created. Provides context for user entry points and helps track navigation patterns and application usage across different interface locations.

referrer.description: Referrer URL that directed to the session creation. Useful for tracking user flow, marketing campaign effectiveness, and understanding how users arrive at the application from external sources.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the session was created. Used for chronological ordering, session lifecycle tracking, and audit trail compliance across security monitoring operations.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the session expired. Null if still active. Used for session validity tracking, automatic session cleanup, and security compliance monitoring of active versus expired sessions.

ITodoAppTodo.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and filtering todo items with security context.

Contains comprehensive search, filter, pagination, and user isolation parameters for secure todo retrieval operations. Supports text search across todo titles and descriptions, date-based filtering for due dates, and standard pagination controls to enable flexible yet secure todo querying.

The operation respects user privacy boundaries by default, filtering by the authenticated user's context automatically. All operations using this schema enforce authentication and validate user ownership of returned todo items.

Used in secure todo list operations to provide clients with powerful filtering capabilities while maintaining strict user isolation and data protection boundaries. This schema integrates with the todo_app_todos table structure to ensure all search parameters align with available database fields and indexing strategies.

search.description: Text search query to filter todos by title or description content. Supports partial matching across todo titles and descriptions using PostgreSQL full-text search capabilities. The search operates on both the title field and description field, returning todos that contain the search terms in either field.

due_before.description: Filter todos with due dates before this timestamp. Useful for finding overdue or upcoming tasks while respecting user ownership boundaries. The filter operates on the due_date field in the todo_app_todos table and excludes todos without due dates unless specifically included in the search criteria.

due_after.description: Filter todos with due dates after this timestamp. Useful for finding future scheduled tasks within the authenticated user's scope. The filter operates on the due_date field and can be combined with due_before to create date range searches for precise todo filtering.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Starts from 1 for the first page of user-filtered todos. The pagination system ensures efficient data retrieval by limiting the number of records returned per request, supporting large todo collections while maintaining performance.

limit.description: Number of items per page for paginated results. Controls the size of each result page within user-owned todo boundaries. The maximum limit of 100 prevents excessive resource consumption while providing sufficient flexibility for most use cases.

id.description: Primary key identifier for the todo item. Unique across all todo records in the system. Generated automatically using UUID v4 upon todo creation and immutable throughout the todo's lifecycle.

user.description: Owner user who created this todo. Provides complete user context including name, avatar, and other essential user information for display purposes. References the todo_app_users table through the todo_app_user_id foreign key relationship.

session.description: User session that created this todo for audit tracing. Links to the authenticated session record for security compliance and audit trail requirements. References the todo_app_user_sessions table through the todo_app_user_session_id foreign key.

title.description: Todo title that briefly describes the task. Required field that provides the primary identification for the todo item in user interfaces. Maximum length of 255 characters ensures concise yet descriptive task identification.

description.description: Detailed description of the todo task. Optional field with maximum length of 1000 characters for comprehensive task documentation. Provides additional context and details beyond the title for complex todo items.

due_date.description: Optional due date for the todo item. Must be in the future if provided, used for scheduling and priority management. Enables time-based todo organization and deadline tracking functionality.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the todo was created. System-managed field that cannot be modified by clients, used for chronological ordering and audit trail compliance. Automatically set to the current timestamp upon todo creation.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the todo was last updated. Automatically maintained by the database to track modification history. Updated whenever any field in the todo record changes, providing accurate change tracking.

deleted_at.description: Timestamp when the todo was soft deleted. Null for active todos, used for recovery capability and data retention compliance. Enables todo restoration while maintaining data integrity through soft deletion patterns.

ITodoAppTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary view of todo item information with complete ownership and audit context.

Provides essential todo details including ownership information, session audit trails, and business data for secure list views and quick references. Includes transformed foreign key relationships to provide complete user and session context in a single API call.

Used when displaying todo items in secure contexts where user ownership validation, audit trail compliance, and complete business data representation are required. Supports proper user isolation and data protection while providing comprehensive todo information for list displays and dashboard views.

This summary variant includes all fields from the todo_app_todos table with appropriate required settings based on Prisma schema nullability constraints. Optional fields like description, due_date, and deleted_at are included but not required, allowing flexible todo representation in summary contexts.

description.description: Detailed description of the todo task. Optional field with maximum length of 1000 characters.

due_date.description: Optional due date for the todo item. Must be in the future if provided.

ITodoAppTodo.ICreate.description:
Request DTO for creating a new todo item.

Contains the essential information needed to create a new todo task. The user ID and session ID are automatically determined from authentication context and should not be provided in the request.

Used when users create new todo items through the application interface, capturing the core task information while maintaining proper ownership and audit trail. Ownership information (user ID and session ID) is automatically assigned from the authenticated user context for security and audit compliance.

description.description: Updated detailed description of the todo task.

ITodoAppTodo.IUpdate.description:
Request DTO for updating an existing todo item.

Allows modification of todo title, description, and due date. Ownership information (user ID and session ID) cannot be changed after creation and is therefore excluded from this update DTO.

All fields are optional, allowing partial updates without requiring all todo information to be resent. Security boundaries ensure users can only modify their own todo items while maintaining immutable ownership context.

ITodoAppTodoLifecycle.description:
Current lifecycle state of todo items for real-time status tracking and mutable state management.

Maintains the present state of each todo item, including current status, priority, and completion information through the referenced snapshot. This schema represents the mutable aspects of todo management while the main todo schema contains immutable attributes, enabling efficient state updates without modifying core todo data.

Each lifecycle record points to the current snapshot via the todo_app_todo_snapshot_id foreign key, ensuring data consistency between real-time state and historical tracking. The system updates this record whenever todo state changes occur, providing efficient access to current todo information without requiring complex historical data queries.

This separation architecture enables high-performance querying for current todo states while maintaining comprehensive audit trails through the snapshot pattern. It supports concurrent todo modifications by isolating mutable state from immutable attributes, ensuring data integrity during simultaneous updates from multiple users.

priority.description: Reference to the new priority for the todo lifecycle. Provides complete priority information including code, name, weight, and active status for validation and sorting purposes.

current_snapshot.description: Reference to the current snapshot representing this state. Links the lifecycle to the specific snapshot record that captures the current todo state.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this lifecycle state was last updated. System-managed field that tracks when the lifecycle was modified for audit purposes.

ITodoAppTodoLifecycle.IUpdate.description:
Update DTO for modifying the current lifecycle state of a todo item.

This schema allows authorized users to modify the current lifecycle state of a todo item, including status changes, priority adjustments, and snapshot updates. When updating the lifecycle state, the system automatically creates a new snapshot to preserve the historical record while updating the current state.

The schema validates that the requested status and priority values are valid according to the reference tables. It ensures that status transitions follow business rules and that priority changes are within acceptable ranges. The current snapshot reference ensures data consistency between the lifecycle state and the historical record.

Security considerations include verifying that the requesting user has ownership or appropriate permissions to modify the todo's lifecycle state. The operation checks that the todo exists and is accessible before applying updates.

This schema integrates with the todo_app_todo_lifecycles table as defined in the Prisma schema, maintaining data consistency between the current state and historical snapshots while supporting real-time todo management workflows.

priority.description: Reference to the todo priority at the time of snapshot creation. Captures the exact priority state including code, name, weight, and active status for historical accuracy.

snapshot_created_at.description: Timestamp when this specific snapshot was created. System-managed field that cannot be modified by clients, used for chronological ordering and audit trail purposes.

ITodoAppTodoSnapshot.description:
Historical snapshot entity capturing point-in-time todo states.

Represents immutable records of todo items at specific moments in their lifecycle. Each snapshot captures the complete mutable state of a todo, including status, priority, and completion status, for audit trails and version control. Snapshots are automatically generated by the system when significant changes occur to todo items.

This entity enables features like undo operations, change history viewing, compliance reporting, and debugging by providing a complete historical record of todo evolution. The temporal nature of snapshots supports time-based queries and temporal data analysis for business intelligence purposes.

The schema maintains proper relationships with todo, status, and priority entities through foreign key references, ensuring data integrity and enabling efficient querying of snapshot information across the entire system.

ITodoAppTodoPriority.ISummary.description:
Summary view of todo priority levels for efficient list displays and UI components.

Provides essential priority information optimized for performance in list views, dropdown selections, and summary displays. Includes only the most critical fields needed for priority identification, sorting, and basic functionality.

The weight field enables automated sorting of todo items by priority level, with lower values indicating higher urgency. The is_active field allows filtering of available priority levels in user interfaces, ensuring users only see currently active priorities for selection.

This summary variant excludes detailed descriptions and complex metadata to minimize payload size while maintaining full functionality for priority-based operations across the application. It is particularly useful in list views and quick reference scenarios where performance is prioritized over comprehensive detail.

created_before.description: Filter snapshots created before this ISO 8601 timestamp. Useful for retrieving older snapshot history or snapshots captured before a specific system event or user action.

ITodoAppTodoSnapshot.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering criteria for retrieving historical todo snapshots with comprehensive audit trail capabilities.

This request DTO enables sophisticated querying of the todo_app_todo_snapshots table, allowing users to search through the complete version history of a todo item. The filtering capabilities support complex queries based on status transitions, priority changes, completion states, and temporal ranges.

The operation integrates with the Prisma schema relationships, ensuring that all filters reference valid foreign key constraints and maintain data integrity. Pagination parameters are optimized for performance while providing flexible access to potentially large historical datasets.

All parameters are optional, enabling both simple paginated browsing and advanced filtered searches. The design supports compliance requirements by providing complete visibility into todo lifecycle changes while maintaining efficient API performance.

id.description: Primary key identifier for the todo snapshot. Automatically generated UUID that uniquely identifies this historical snapshot record in the system.

todo_app_todo_id.description: Reference to the original todo item that this snapshot captures. Foreign key relationship to the todo_app_todos table, establishing the connection between the snapshot and its originating todo.

todo_app_todo_status_id.description: Foreign key reference to the status at the time of snapshot creation. Links to the todo_app_todo_statuses table to capture the exact status state when this snapshot was recorded.

todo_app_todo_priority_id.description: Foreign key reference to the priority at the time of snapshot creation. Links to the todo_app_todo_priorities table to capture the priority setting when this snapshot was taken.

status.description: Summary information about the status at the time of snapshot creation. Provides a lightweight reference to the status entity with essential display information for user interfaces.

priority.description: Summary information about the priority at the time of snapshot creation. Provides a compact reference to the priority entity with key information needed for display and sorting purposes.

completed_at.description: Timestamp when the todo was marked as completed in this snapshot. Null if the todo was not completed at the time this snapshot was created. Captures the completion state for historical tracking and audit purposes.

snapshot_created_at.description: Timestamp when this specific snapshot was created. Records the exact moment when the system captured this point-in-time state of the todo item for version control and audit trail purposes.

ITodoAppTodoSnapshot.ISummary.description:
Summary view of historical todo snapshots for list displays and UI cards.

Provides a lightweight representation of todo snapshots optimized for paginated lists and summary views. Includes essential information about the snapshot while referencing related entities through summary objects to avoid data duplication and maintain context.

This summary view supports efficient browsing of historical todo changes while maintaining the relationships between snapshots and their associated status and priority information. The structure enables quick loading of snapshot lists with sufficient context for user understanding.

id.description: Primary key identifier for the todo status. Generated automatically using UUID v4 when a new status definition is created in the system.

code.description: Unique status code used for system identification and API operations. This code serves as the primary business identifier for the status and must be unique across all status definitions. Examples include: 'pending', 'in-progress', 'completed'.

name.description: Descriptive status name for user interface display. Provides a human-readable label that appears in dropdowns, filters, and status indicators throughout the application interface.

description.description: Detailed explanation of what this status represents and its business meaning. Optional field that provides context about when this status should be used and what it signifies in the todo lifecycle.

is_active.description: Indicates whether this status is currently available for use in the system. Inactive statuses are preserved for historical reference but cannot be assigned to new todo items or used in active workflows.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this status definition was created in the system. Automatically set when the status record is first inserted into the database.

ITodoAppTodoStatus.description:
Reference entity defining valid todo status values for the Todo application.

This entity provides a normalized set of status options that todos can transition through during their lifecycle, ensuring consistent status handling across the system while enabling easy extension and customization of status workflows.

Status definitions control the permitted state transitions and business rules for todo management. The entity supports internationalization and user interface customization through descriptive names and explanations while maintaining system integrity through standardized codes.

Using a reference table instead of hardcoded enum values provides flexibility for future status additions and maintains data integrity through foreign key constraints, separating business logic from database schema for better maintainability and extensibility.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-based index). Controls which page of results to retrieve from the paginated dataset. Defaults to 1 if not specified.

limit.description: Number of items per page for pagination. Determines how many status records to return in each page of results. Defaults to 20 if not specified, with a maximum limit of 100 records per page.

search.description: Search term to filter statuses by name or description content. Supports partial matching across text fields. Case-insensitive search that matches any part of the name or description fields.

code.description: Filter statuses by exact code match. Useful for retrieving specific status definitions by their unique identifier. Provides precise filtering for administrative operations.

is_active.description: Filter statuses by active/inactive status. Allows separating currently available statuses from historical definitions. When specified, returns only statuses matching the specified active state.

codes.description: Filter statuses by multiple code values. Supports retrieving a specific set of status definitions in a single query. Useful for bulk operations or preloading commonly used status sets.

ITodoAppTodoPriority.description:

The reference table pattern allows for easy extension of priority options and maintains data integrity through foreign key constraints. It supports customization of priority systems for different user preferences or organizational needs.

By normalizing priorities, the system achieves better data consistency and enables features like priority-based filtering, sorting, and notification systems without hardcoded business logic in the schema.

ITodoAppTodoPriority.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering parameters for querying todo priority levels.

This request DTO provides comprehensive filtering capabilities for administrators to search and manage the todo priority classification system. It supports pagination for handling large sets of priority definitions and multiple filtering options to narrow down results based on specific criteria.

The search functionality enables administrators to find priorities by their code or name, while the active status filter allows reviewing both current and historical priority definitions. Sorting options provide flexibility in how priorities are presented, with weight-based sorting being particularly useful for understanding the priority hierarchy.

This DTO is designed for administrative interfaces where comprehensive priority management is required, supporting both broad overviews and targeted searches within the priority classification system.

total_todos.description:
Total number of todos owned by the authenticated user.

This count includes all todos regardless of their current status or priority level. It represents the complete set of tasks the user has created and manages within the system.

The count is calculated by querying the todo_app_todos table filtered by the authenticated user's ID. This ensures users can only see their own todo statistics for privacy and security purposes.

This metric provides a baseline for understanding the user's overall task management workload and serves as the denominator for calculating completion rates and other productivity metrics.

completed_todos.description:
Number of todos that have been marked as completed.

This count represents todos that have reached a completed status, indicating finished tasks. The calculation considers the current status from todo_app_todo_lifecycles table joined with todo_app_todo_statuses where the status code indicates completion.

Completed todos contribute to productivity metrics and help users track their accomplishment rate. This count excludes todos that are pending, in-progress, or in any other non-completed state.

The system ensures that only the authenticated user's completed todos are counted, maintaining data isolation and privacy across different user accounts.

pending_todos.description:
Number of todos that are currently in a pending state.

Pending todos represent tasks that have been created but not yet started. This count is calculated by querying the todo_app_todo_lifecycles table for todos with a pending status code, filtered by the authenticated user's ownership.

This metric helps users understand their backlog of unstarted tasks and provides insight into potential workload management needs. Pending todos are typically the next candidates for action in the user's workflow.

The count is updated in real-time as todos transition between different status states, providing accurate current state information for dashboard display.

in_progress_todos.description:
Number of todos that are currently being actively worked on.

In-progress todos represent tasks that have been started but not yet completed. This count is calculated from the todo_app_todo_lifecycles table filtered by the in-progress status code and the authenticated user's ownership.

This metric indicates the user's current active workload and helps balance task distribution. It provides insight into how many concurrent tasks the user is handling at any given time.

The count dynamically updates as todos transition between status states, ensuring the dashboard reflects real-time work-in-progress information.

overdue_todos.description:
Number of todo items that have passed their due date.

This count represents todos that are overdue, helping users identify tasks that require immediate attention. The calculation queries the todo_app_todos table for todos with due dates that have passed, filtered by the authenticated user's ownership and excluding completed todos.

Overdue todos provide critical visibility into time-sensitive commitments that may be at risk. This metric supports proactive task management by highlighting deadlines that have been missed and require resolution.

The system ensures accurate overdue tracking by comparing current datetime with todo due dates, providing real-time visibility into deadline compliance status.

priority_distribution.description:
Distribution of todos across different priority levels.

This object provides a breakdown of how the user's todos are distributed across the available priority classifications (low, medium, high). The counts are calculated by joining the todo_app_todo_lifecycles table with todo_app_todo_priorities reference table.

The priority distribution helps users understand the urgency mix of their current workload and supports effective priority-based task management. It enables quick assessment of whether the user's task portfolio is balanced or skewed toward specific urgency levels.

This information is particularly valuable for workload planning, resource allocation, and identifying potential areas where priority rebalancing might be beneficial for optimal productivity outcomes.

completion_rate.description:
Percentage of todos that have been completed relative to the total number of todos.

This metric is calculated as (completed_todos / total_todos) * 100, providing a clear percentage representation of completion progress. It offers a high-level view of the user's overall productivity and task completion effectiveness.

The completion rate helps users track their accomplishment patterns over time and serves as a key performance indicator for personal productivity management. It automatically updates as todos are completed or new todos are added to the system.

This percentage is rounded to two decimal places for precise tracking and is bounded between 0% (no todos completed) and 100% (all todos completed), providing a normalized metric for comparison and trend analysis.

average_completion_time_hours.description:
Average time taken to complete todo items in hours.

This metric calculates the average duration between todo creation and completion across all completed todos. The calculation uses timestamps from todo_app_todos.created_at and todo_app_todo_snapshots.completed_at fields to determine completion timeframes.

Average completion time provides insight into the user's typical task completion efficiency and helps identify patterns in productivity rhythms. It supports performance benchmarking and trend analysis for continuous improvement in task management effectiveness.

The metric is calculated only for completed todos and excludes ongoing or pending tasks, ensuring accurate measurement of actual completion performance rather than projected timelines.

recent_completions.description:
Number of todos completed within the recent timeframe (typically last 7 days).

This count represents the user's recent productivity activity by tracking todos that were marked as completed within a defined recent period. The calculation queries the todo_app_todo_snapshots table for completion events within the specified timeframe, filtered by the authenticated user's ownership.

Recent completions provide insight into the user's current productivity trends and help identify patterns in task completion behavior. This metric is particularly valuable for understanding short-term productivity fluctuations and recent accomplishment patterns.

The timeframe for 'recent' is typically configured as the last 7 days, but may be adjustable based on system configuration or user preferences for different analytical perspectives.

upcoming_due_dates.description:
Number of todos with due dates approaching within the near future (typically next 7 days).

This count represents todos that have upcoming deadlines, helping users identify time-sensitive tasks that require attention. The calculation queries the todo_app_todos table for todos with due dates falling within the defined upcoming period, filtered by the authenticated user's ownership and excluding already completed todos.

Upcoming due dates provide proactive workload management by highlighting impending deadlines before they become critical. This metric supports effective time management and priority planning by identifying time-sensitive tasks that need to be addressed in the near future.

The timeframe for 'upcoming' is typically configured as the next 7 days, providing a reasonable planning horizon for most task management scenarios while maintaining focus on immediate priorities.

ITodoAppTodoDashboard.description:
Comprehensive dashboard overview containing aggregated todo statistics and metrics for the authenticated user.

This dashboard provides a high-level summary of the user's todo management system, aggregating data from multiple database tables to present key performance indicators and productivity metrics. It serves as the central overview for users to quickly assess their task management status and identify areas needing attention.

The dashboard integrates information from todo_app_todos for basic todo counts and due date tracking, todo_app_todo_lifecycles for current state tracking, todo_app_todo_statuses for status definitions, todo_app_todo_priorities for classification data, and todo_app_todo_snapshots for completion timing analysis. This multi-source approach ensures comprehensive and accurate metric calculation.

Security is maintained through strict user-based data isolation, ensuring that each user only sees their own todo statistics. The dashboard automatically filters all data based on the authenticated user's identity extracted from the JWT token.

This overview supports effective task management by providing visibility into workload distribution, completion patterns, priority balancing, overdue commitments, and upcoming deadlines. It enables users to make informed decisions about task prioritization, resource allocation, and productivity optimization strategies.

date_range.description:
Date range filter for limiting analytics to a specific time period.

This object allows users to define a custom date range for their todo analytics, enabling focused analysis of specific time periods. The date range filter is applied to completion timestamps and status change events recorded in the todo_app_todo_snapshots table.

By specifying a date range, users can analyze productivity patterns during specific periods, compare performance across different timeframes, or focus on recent activity for current assessment. The system ensures that only data within the specified range is included in the analytical calculations.

If no date range is provided, the system may apply default time boundaries based on typical analytical requirements, such as analyzing the past 30 days or the current calendar month.

items.description:
Specific status codes to include in the analytics.

This array allows users to filter analytics results to include only todos that transitioned through specific status values. Valid status codes are defined in the todo_app_todo_statuses reference table (e.g., 'pending', 'in-progress', 'completed').

Status filtering enables focused analysis on specific workflow stages or transition patterns. For example, users might analyze only completion patterns by filtering for the 'completed' status, or examine workflow bottlenecks by focusing on specific status transitions.

If no status filters are specified, the analytics include todos regardless of their status, providing a comprehensive view of all todo activity within the specified date range.

status_filters.description:
Array of status codes to filter the analytics results.

This optional filter allows users to narrow their analytics to specific todo status transitions. By specifying one or more status codes, users can focus their analysis on particular aspects of their workflow, such as completion patterns, pending task analysis, or in-progress work tracking.

The status codes must match valid values from the todo_app_todo_statuses reference table. The analytics will include only todos that had the specified status transitions within the defined date range.

This filtering capability supports targeted analytical queries that address specific productivity questions or workflow optimization needs, providing more precise insights than broad, unfiltered analytics.

items.description:
Specific priority codes to include in the analytics.

This array allows users to filter analytics results to include only todos with specific priority levels. Valid priority codes are defined in the todo_app_todo_priorities reference table (e.g., 'low', 'medium', 'high').

Priority filtering enables analysis of how different urgency levels affect completion patterns and productivity. Users can examine whether high-priority tasks are completed more efficiently, or analyze the distribution of completion times across different priority levels.

If no priority filters are specified, the analytics include todos of all priority levels, providing a comprehensive view of productivity across the entire priority spectrum.

priority_filters.description:
Array of priority codes to filter the analytics results.

This optional filter allows users to narrow their analytics to specific todo priority levels. By specifying one or more priority codes, users can analyze productivity patterns specific to different urgency classifications.

The priority codes must match valid values from the todo_app_todo_priorities reference table. The analytics will include only todos that had the specified priority levels during the analyzed timeframe.

This filtering supports priority-based productivity analysis, helping users understand how task urgency influences completion rates, time-to-completion metrics, and overall workflow efficiency for different classes of tasks.

- 'same_day': Todos completed on the same day they were created
- 'within_week': Todos completed within 7 days of creation
- 'within_month': Todos completed within 30 days of creation
- 'extended': Todos that took more than 30 days to complete

Pattern filtering enables analysis of productivity timing characteristics, helping users understand their typical completion timeframes and identify potential areas for workflow optimization.

This parameter controls which page of analytics results to return when the data set is large enough to require pagination. Page numbers start at 1, with the first page containing the initial set of results.

Pagination ensures that large analytics datasets can be processed efficiently without overwhelming system resources or client applications. Each page typically contains a manageable number of records for display and analysis.

If not specified, the system defaults to returning the first page of results. Users can navigate through subsequent pages by incrementing this parameter to access different segments of the analytical data.

Number of results to return per page.

This parameter specifies how many analytics records to include on each page of results. The limit helps control the volume of data returned in a single response, ensuring efficient processing and manageable data transfer.

ITodoAppTodoAnalytics.IRequest.description:
Analytics search criteria including date ranges, filters, and pagination parameters for todo completion pattern analysis.

This request object defines the parameters for searching and analyzing todo completion patterns through advanced filtering capabilities. It enables users to perform targeted analytical queries that focus on specific aspects of their productivity and task management behaviors.

The criteria support complex filtering by date ranges, status transitions, priority levels, and completion timing patterns. This flexibility allows users to answer specific productivity questions and gain insights into particular workflow characteristics.

Security is maintained by automatically applying user-based filtering to ensure that analytics only reflect the authenticated user's own todo data. The request parameters are validated against the user's accessible data scope to prevent unauthorized analytical queries.

Pagination parameters ensure that large analytical datasets can be processed efficiently, with configurable page sizes and navigation controls. The system optimizes query performance for complex analytical operations while maintaining data accuracy and completeness.

total_todos.description: Total number of todo items across all statuses for the authenticated user. This count includes all active todos that have not been soft deleted (deleted_at is null). The value is always non-negative and reflects the current workload based on user access permissions.

completed_todos.description: Number of todo items marked as completed status. This count specifically tracks todos that have reached the completed state as defined in the todo_app_todo_statuses reference table. The value represents current completion rate for performance analysis.

pending_todos.description: Number of todo items currently in pending status awaiting action. This metric helps users understand their backlog and prioritize work based on items that haven't been started yet.

in_progress_todos.description: Number of todo items actively being worked on in the in-progress status. This real-time metric indicates current workload intensity and helps with resource allocation and time management decisions.

overdue_todos.description: Number of todo items that have passed their due_date without being completed. This critical metric identifies time-sensitive tasks that require immediate attention and helps prevent deadline violations.

average_completion_time_hours.description: Average time taken to complete todo items in hours, calculated from creation to completion timestamps. This performance metric helps users understand their productivity patterns and set realistic expectations for future task completion.

priority_distribution.description: Distribution of todo items across different priority levels (low, medium, high) as defined in the todo_app_todo_priorities reference table. This breakdown provides insights into workload urgency and helps with strategic task prioritization.

The metrics support strategic decision-making by highlighting workload distribution, identifying bottlenecks, and tracking performance improvement over time. All data is filtered based on the authenticated user's permissions and access scope, ensuring data security and privacy compliance.

This analytics entity enables users to understand their productivity patterns, set realistic goals, and optimize their todo management workflow for maximum efficiency and effectiveness.

IDateRange.description:
Date range filter for limiting analytics to a specific time period.

This object allows users to define a custom date range for their todo analytics, enabling focused analysis of specific time periods. The date range filter is applied to completion timestamps and status change events recorded in the todo_app_todo_snapshots table.

By specifying a date range, users can analyze productivity patterns during specific periods, compare performance across different timeframes, or focus on recent activity for current assessment. The system ensures that only data within the specified range is included in the analytical calculations.

If no date range is provided, the system may apply default time boundaries based on typical analytical requirements, such as analyzing the past 30 days or the current calendar month.

start_date.description:
Start date for the analytics time period.

This field specifies the beginning of the date range for analyzing todo completion patterns. The analytics will include todos that were completed or had status changes occurring on or after this date.

The date should be provided in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) to ensure proper timezone handling and date parsing. If not specified, the system may use a default range based on typical analytical needs.

This parameter enables users to focus their analysis on specific time periods, such as recent weeks, specific months, or custom date ranges that align with their productivity assessment goals.

end_date.description:
End date for the analytics time period.

This field specifies the conclusion of the date range for analyzing todo completion patterns. The analytics will include todos that were completed or had status changes occurring on or before this date.

The date should be provided in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ) to ensure consistent timezone handling. If not specified, the system typically uses the current date as the endpoint for the analysis.

Combined with the start_date, this parameter defines the complete timeframe for analytical queries, enabling focused analysis of specific productivity periods or historical trend examination.
